Teamcenter\-X Procedures

This document is formal guideline to setup the basic framework for getting the virtual machines deployed in an Azure subscription \(manually / through the TcX pipeline\) patched in an automated manner\. We are leveraging Azure policies and Azure Update Manager services for this purpose\. The document also includes steps to set up an automated reporting mechanism for this purpose\.

##### Policy Tag

[Siemens Industry Software \(SISW\) SaaS Access Control Policy\.pdf](#_References)

##### Scope

- Policies to apply on the Management Group/Subscription\.
- Maintenance Window to configure to dynamically select the machines for patching\.
- Logic Apps to configure for ensuring automated reports getting sent out to relevant stakeholders post patching operation\.

## <a id="_Toc169694251"></a>Principles

The patching solution covers the below principles as part of its implementation\.

- Policy to tag the virtual machines with a tag : __Patch=True__
- Policy to set the Patch Orchestration Mode of the virtual machines to Customer Managed Schedules\. This ensures that the updates on the machine are applied only through customer defined maintenance configuration windows\.
- Azure Update Manager Maintenance Configuration windows\. This ensures the correct set of machines matching the required criteria is picked up for updated through the update Manager service\. The type of updates to be installed can also be configured using this\.
- If the user wants to exclude his/her machine from the automated patching exercise__, they need to change the tag value of Patch from True to False__\. This would ensure that the machine is not picked up by the Update Manager for updating\.

## <a id="_Toc137544288"></a><a id="_Toc138404965"></a><a id="_Toc169694252"></a>Roles and Responsibilities

The user should have sufficient access to apply the policies and configure the Maintenance Configurations window\. 

If the user is planning to apply the same across multiple subscriptions , then the user should have sufficient privileges to select all the subs in dynamic scopes\.

## <a id="_Toc169694253"></a>Procedures

__Please follow the below mentioned steps to ensure that your VM’s are automatically patched through Azure Update Manager:__ 

__Apply the below mentioned polices :__ 

1. __Tag all virtual machines with Patch=True tag__ 

This policy ensures that all the machines deployed in the subscription are with tagged with the value Patch=True 

__Policy Name: Tag all virtual machines deployed for inclusion in scope of recurring update via Azure Update Manager service __

__Below is the policy definition for the same: __

__![](data:image/x-emf;base64,)__

1. __Set the patch orchestration mode to Customer Managed Schedules for the Linux virtual machines\. __

This policy ensures that the patch orchestration mode on the Linux virtual machines is set to Customer Managed Schedules\.

__Policy name:  \[tcx\] Configure Linux virtual machines for recurring updates via AUM through customer defined windows\. __

__Below is the policy definition for the same:__

__![](data:image/x-emf;base64,)__

1. __Set the Patch orchestration mode to Customer Managed Schedules for the Windows virtual machines\. __

This policy ensures that the patch orchestration mode on the Linux virtual machines is set to Customer Managed Schedules

__Policy Name: \[tcx\] Configure windows virtual machines for recurring updates via AUM through customer defined windows\. __

__![](data:image/x-emf;base64,)__

__Configure Maintenance Configuration Windows: __

The maintenance configuration window  is configured to create specific user\-defined windows which would be leveraged by the Azure Update Manager to update the machines with the resp patches configured\. 

As per the current configuration in Non\-Prod, we are having 2 maintenance configuration windows which are updating Linux and Windows machines respectively \.They are each running on Saturday’s and Sundays respectively at 5 pm IST\.

__*12\] Give the parameters and query to get the report * __

__We have 3 scenarios __

__a\. *The sample query to get list of all the machines which succeeded in patch installation:* __

__arg\(''\)\.patchinstallationresources   
| where type in~ \("microsoft\.compute/virtualmachines/patchinstallationresults", "microsoft\.hybridcompute/machines/patchinstallationresults"\)   
| where properties\.status =~ "Succeeded" // "CompletedWithWarnings" and other statuses can also be considered   
| where properties\.lastModifiedDateTime > ago\(6d\)   
| extend machineName = tostring\(split\(id, '/', 8\)\)   
| where properties\.maintenanceRunId contains "tcxonazure\_linuxweeklypatching"   
| parse id with vmResourceId "/patchInstallationResults" \*   
| parse machineName with VM\_name   
| parse subscriptionId with Subscription   
| parse properties\.status with vmStatus   
| parse resourceGroup with resourcegroup   
| parse properties\.lastModifiedDateTime with Date\_and\_Time   
| project VM\_name, vmStatus, Date\_and\_Time, resourcegroup, Subscription   
| distinct VM\_name, vmStatus, Date\_and\_Time, resourcegroup, Subscription __

__b\. *The sample query to get list of all the machines which failed in patch installation:* __

__arg\(''\)\.patchinstallationresources   
| where type in~ \("microsoft\.compute/virtualmachines/patchinstallationresults", "microsoft\.hybridcompute/machines/patchinstallationresults"\)   
| where properties\.status =~ "Failed" // "CompletedWithWarnings" and other statuses can also be considered   
| where properties\.lastModifiedDateTime > ago\(6d\)   
| extend machineName = tostring\(split\(id, '/', 8\)\)   
| where properties\.maintenanceRunId contains "tcxonazure\_linuxweeklypatching"   
| parse id with vmResourceId "/patchInstallationResults" \*   
| parse machineName with VM\_name   
| parse subscriptionId with Subscription   
| parse properties\.status with vmStatus   
| parse resourceGroup with resourcegroup   
| parse properties\.lastModifiedDateTime with Date\_and\_Time   
| project VM\_name, vmStatus, Date\_and\_Time, resourcegroup, Subscription   
| distinct VM\_name, vmStatus, Date\_and\_Time, resourcegroup, Subscription __

__c\. *The sample query to get list of all the machines which were excluded in patch installation:* __

__arg\(''\)\.resources   
| where type == "microsoft\.compute/virtualmachines"   
| where tags\.Patch =~ "False"    
| where properties\.storageProfile\.osDisk\.osType =~ 'Linux'   
| parse name with VM\_Name __

__| parse subscriptionId with Subscription   
| parse tags with Tags   
| parse resourceGroup with Resource\_group   
| project VM\_Name ,Subscription, Tags , Resource\_group __
